meta.description: Draw and export phylogenetic trees with Bio.Phylo plus matplotlib, and route rich figures to ggtree, ETE4, or iTOL.
meta.executed: 9/9 inputs executed (Biopython 1.88 + matplotlib in audit-envs/molecular-phylogenetics-analyst; R via rrun.ps1 with ggtree 3.14.0, ggplot2 4.0.3, treeio 1.30.0, ggtreeExtra 1.16.0, ape 5.8.1)
meta.execution_note: Third audit of this Skill (78 -> 84 -> this pass). Fix under test: commit 4cc2487 (fail-loud ValueError on MRCA clade mismatch), on top of the Backlog-pass commits (fa75880 root-before-MRCA, 00141d5 gheatmap wording, 0f50878 ggtree rich-figure recipe) which the 84-score audit's BACKLOG.md had stale-listed as still open. All 9 inputs from the 84-score report re-run as regression at HEAD; 2 of them (Input 2, Input 5) rebuilt from scratch as direct fix-verification rather than re-using the prior auditor's scripts. Data: SYNTHETIC (data/make_data.py, reused from prior audit) plus real IQ-TREE/BEAST fixture outputs already checked into audits/bio-phylo-tree-visualization/data/.

scientific_integrity.detail: All figures drawn from synthetic or already-public reference trees (primates16, beast_mcc); no fabricated statistics.

practice_boundaries.detail: Figure-drawing scope only; no diagnostic or prescriptive content.

methodological_ground.detail: Skill actively prevents methodological fallacies: support-scale conflation, basal claims on unrooted layouts, ladderization-as-progress, chronograms without HPD bars. The MRCA-mismatch guard (this fix) is itself a methodological-fallacy prevention.

code_usability.detail: Every Bio.Phylo and ggtree/treeio recipe in SKILL.md ran to completion on real or synthetic fixtures; documented version-specific failures (ggtree layouts, gheatmap) reproduced exactly as stated.

functional_suitability.note: All three functional_suitability gaps from the 84-score audit are now resolved and independently re-verified by execution: MRCA colour recipe roots first and fails loudly on a genuine miss; the gheatmap version-block line matches reproduced behaviour exactly; the ggtree rich-figure recipe runs end to end on real IQ-TREE output. Held at 11/12, not 12, because a closely related failure mode (no clade has ANY readable support) is still a print-only warning while the MRCA-mismatch path is now a hard raise -- an inconsistency in severity between two adjacent recipes.

reliability.note: The new ValueError gives a specific, actionable message (names the outgroup/rooting check to make) and was verified to fire only on the genuine bug path, never on the correct rooted path -- a real fault-tolerance improvement. Held at 11 because the sibling 'no support' warning is not yet a hard stop for consistency.

performance_context.note: 288 lines (up from 245 with the added ggtree recipe section), still well under the 500-line budget; references/examples carry depth appropriately.

agent_usability.note: The colour recipe's rooting caveat is now wired directly into the code path (root-first instruction immediately precedes the guarded common_ancestor call) rather than living only in the Common Errors table, closing the gap the 84-score audit flagged.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger prompts; unchanged from prior audit.

security.note: All outputs write to temp/namespaced paths; no credential or unsanitized-input exposure. Unchanged.

maintainability.note: labeled_tree.py exercises dual-support parsing but prints no asserted expected output; unchanged from prior audit.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger description and clean routing to tree-io/tree-manipulation; unchanged from prior audit.

recommendations.title: Inconsistent failure severity between two adjacent recipes
recommendations.problem: The MRCA-mismatch guard now raises ValueError, but the closely related 'no clade has any readable support' case one recipe above it is still a print-only warning.
recommendations.root_cause: The two guards were hardened in separate fix passes without reconciling severity.
recommendations.fix: Either raise on both conditions or explicitly note in the Common Errors table why one is a hard stop and the other is a warning.

recommendations.title: Bio.Phylo panel remains illegible well above the documented threshold
recommendations.problem: Even with the height cap and the >150-tip warning, the Bio.Phylo rectangular panel at 320 tips cannot itself produce legible tip labels.
recommendations.root_cause: Bio.Phylo/matplotlib has no radial or ring layout to relieve label density; this is a tool ceiling, not a recipe bug.
recommendations.fix: Consider having the recipe refuse to render past a hard cap (e.g. ~200 tips) and require the ggtree/iTOL route instead of producing a technically-successful but illegible figure.

recommendations.title: ape unrooted fallback has no worked code recipe with a scale bar
recommendations.problem: The ape::plot.phylo(type='unrooted') fallback is a one-line mention in the Version Compatibility block, not a full recipe, and omits add.scale.bar.
recommendations.root_cause: The fallback was added as a stopgap note rather than a first-class recipe.
recommendations.fix: Add a short ape unrooted code block alongside the ggtree recipes, including add.scale.bar().
